s1d: It reads your GPUs (NVIDIA, Intel Arc Pro, AMD) or an AVX2 CPU, and measures your RAM and disk.
s2d: Every recipe was run on that exact card and passed six checks: it loads, answers, thinks, calls a tool, recalls a code from a nearly full context window, and decodes at 15 tok/s or more.
s3d: It downloads from Hugging Face at a pinned commit and checks every file's size and sha256 before anything runs.
sXText: New recipes, benchmarks and videos as they happen.

s4d: The engine (SGLang, vLLM, ExLlamaV3 or llama.cpp) runs from an image pinned by digest, behind a keyed gateway on 127.0.0.1 that speaks the OpenAI, Anthropic and Responses APIs.
s5d: Claude Code, Codex, pi, OpenCode, Hermes and more start pointed at your model. Their own config is never touched.
s6t: Fits big models on small machines
s6d: Mixture-of-experts models can keep their experts in RAM or on NVMe: GLM-5.3-Flash passed the lab on one RTX 3090 at 20 tok/s.
cText: Sybil AI is open source, and the registry grows from people running models on their own cards. Pick a way in.
c1d: Run a recipe on your GPU with the registry lab (lab.py try --on endpoint) and open a pull request with the result.
c2t: Share a launch you already run
c2d: Published a working launch with your numbers? It comes in as a reported recipe, credited to your repo, until the six checks run.
c3d: Bugs, a card that shows Coming soon, a new agent to open: issues and pull requests are open.
wLede: Sybil AI turns the computer you already own into a private AI server. It knows which open models run well on your exact card, starts one for you, and points your coding agent at it.
w1d: An NVIDIA, Intel Arc or AMD card, or just a CPU with enough RAM. It reads what you have.
w2d: Picked from recipes tested on that exact card, downloaded at a pinned commit and checked file by file.
w3d: Claude Code, Codex, pi or OpenCode talk to the model on 127.0.0.1. No account, no API bill, nothing sent out.
nTested: passed six checks on the card
vLede: Models running on real cards in the lab: the hardware, the speed and the setup, recorded as they happen. New ones go up on X first.
